29 An outdoor concert has two large speakers beside the stage for broadcasting music.
In order to test the speakers, they are made to emit sound of the same wavelength and the same
amplitude.
The curved lines in the diagram represent wavefronts.
Where is the loudest sound heard?
A
C
D
B
speakers
stage

hints: Look at the curved lines as wavefronts where the displacement is maximum, and see which of points A, B, C and D sits exactly where two curves cross.
Loudest sound means largest resultant amplitude from the two coherent sound waves, which needs constructive interference with path difference $n\lambda$.
Compare the positions: a crossing of two wavefronts means crest meets crest from the two speakers, while a point on only one wavefront or between wavefronts does not satisfy this.
walkthrough: The two speakers emit sound of the same wavelength and amplitude, so they act as two coherent sources that produce a two-source interference pattern.
Loudest sound is heard where the two waves arrive in phase and interfere constructively, giving maximum resultant amplitude.
For wavefront diagrams, constructive interference occurs where a crest from one source meets a crest from the other source, which is seen as the intersection of two wavefront curves.
Check each point: A, B and C do not lie exactly on the crossing of a left-speaker wavefront and a right-speaker wavefront, so the two waves are not fully in phase there.
Point D lies exactly at the crossing of two wavefronts, one centred on each speaker, so the path difference from the two speakers is $n\lambda$ and the displacements add.
Therefore maximum amplitude and loudest sound is at D. This is option D

A.explanation: Point A lies on a wavefront from one speaker but between wavefronts from the other, so the two displacements do not add fully in phase.

B.explanation: Point B lies between wavefronts from both speakers, so it is not at a double crest and does not give maximum constructive interference.

C.explanation: Point C lies close to but not exactly on the crossing of two wavefronts, so the path difference is not $n\lambda$ and the sound is not loudest.

D.explanation: Point D is where a wavefront from the left speaker crosses a wavefront from the right speaker, giving constructive interference and maximum amplitude.
